observations.text: SP maintained basic A/C control at the desired standard for this training block, with the IP directing part of the trim sequence as expected at this stage. Altitude excursions reached 400 feet and airspeed excursions 25 knots in straight and level flight before IP inputs restored the parameters. Marginal performance for the Training Section - the periods of unassisted control lengthened during the second half of the sortie, and a more regular cross check of the control and performance instruments is expected to improve the retention of altitude and airspeed.

SP maintained positive and smooth A/C control in straight and level flight and in turns up to 60 degrees of bank using only the IP's verbal indications, without any IP control input. Altitude deviations were contained at 300 feet, airspeed deviations at 20 knots and exit headings at 10 degrees, recognized and corrected with delay after prompting. The aileron, elevator and rudder trim were set on request and the cross check was re-established each time. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained positive and smooth A/C control throughout the area work and executed the corresponding corrections without IP's intervention. Minor errors produced altitude deviations of 200 feet, airspeed deviations of 15 knots and exit headings 8 degrees off the briefed value, all recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner. The A/C was trimmed after each airspeed change and kept within operational limits. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained positive and smooth A/C control with accuracy and speed, trimming the A/C in detail through the full airspeed range. In straight and level flight and in turns up to 60 degrees of bank the altitude was held within 100 feet, the airspeed within 7 knots and the exit heading within 4 degrees. The cross check of the control and performance instruments was continuous and all corrections were applied without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP handled the aileron, elevator and rudder trim with ease and without any difficulty through the full airspeed range and maintained positive and smooth A/C control in all flight phases. Deviations were negligible, with altitude held within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees. The cross check was uninterrupted, erroneous instrument readings were located in time and reported to the IP, and no procedure was skipped. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a trim technique that relied on holding control pressures instead of trimming the A/C in detail after each airspeed change, did not maintain positive and smooth A/C control in turns up to 60 degrees of bank. Altitude excursions reached 400 feet and the exit heading was 15 degrees off the briefed value, with the result that the IP took the controls and re-established the parameters. Repetition of the trim sequence through the full airspeed range is required.

SP, due to attention captured by a minor system indication while the aircraft state went unmonitored, did not check continuously the indications from the control and performance instruments during straight and level flight. Airspeed decayed by 30 knots and altitude by 400 feet before the deviation was noticed, with the result that the IP directed the recovery and executed part of the level-off. Re-establishing the cross check before addressing any secondary indication is required.

SP maintained basic A/C control within the desired standards for this training block, completing straight and level flight and turns up to 60 degrees of bank after the IP's verbal indications and without any IP control input. Altitude deviations reached 300 feet and airspeed deviations 20 knots, recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - the deviations were smaller in the last two turns, and earlier recognition through a faster instrument cross check is expected to improve.

SP maintained positive and smooth A/C control in straight and level flight and in turns up to 60 degrees of bank without IP's intervention. Small errors in pitch and bank produced altitude deviations of 200 feet, airspeed deviations of 15 knots and exit headings 7 degrees off, all recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner. The A/C was trimmed after each configuration and airspeed change and kept within operational limits. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained positive and smooth A/C control with accuracy and speed, handling the aileron, elevator and rudder trim with ease through the full airspeed range. Altitude was held within 120 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and exit headings within 4 degrees in turns up to 60 degrees of bank. Corrections were applied promptly on the basis of a continuous comparison of the instrument indications with the A/C positioning in space, without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained positive and smooth A/C control in all flight phases with exceptional accuracy, trimming the A/C in detail so that control pressures were released throughout the airspeed range. Altitude was held within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees. The cross check was uninterrupted, all A/C levers and switches were used without any difficulty, and the A/C was kept well within operational limits. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to control inputs applied in large steps instead of the smooth pressures required for positive A/C control, over-controlled the A/C in turns up to 60 degrees of bank and did not trim it after the airspeed changes. Altitude excursions reached 450 feet and airspeed excursions 30 knots, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls to return the A/C within operational limits. The maneuver was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not check continuously the indications from the control and performance instruments and did not execute the corresponding corrections. The A/C descended 400 feet below the assigned altitude with the airspeed 25 knots high and the heading 20 degrees off, with the result that the IP directed the recovery and executed part of the level-off. Shedding the secondary task and returning to the cross check is required before the next sortie.

SP, due to a cross check that dwelt on a single instrument instead of comparing the control and performance indications with the A/C positioning in space, did not locate the developing deviations in time during straight and level flight. Altitude reached 300 feet low and airspeed 20 knots below the briefed value, with the result that the parameters were regained only after the IP's verbal indications, with recognition and correction delayed. No IP control input was required.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic during the area work, did not maintain positive and smooth A/C control and did not trim the A/C after the power change. The exit heading was 10 degrees off and the altitude 300 feet high, with the result that the SP recognized and corrected the deviations with delay, after the IP's verbal indications. Prioritizing A/C control over the secondary task is expected.

SP maintained basic A/C control within the desired standards for this training block, executing the corresponding corrections without IP's intervention. Altitude deviations of 200 feet and airspeed deviations of 15 knots occurred three times in turns up to 60 degrees of bank, each recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - the deviations decreased over the sortie, and more detailed trimming after each airspeed change is expected to improve the consistency of the parameters.

SP maintained positive and smooth A/C control with accuracy and speed, trimming the A/C in detail in all flight phases. Altitude was held within 100 feet, airspeed within 6 knots and exit headings within 3 degrees in straight and level flight and in turns up to 60 degrees of bank. Deviations were located through a continuous cross check and corrected without IP's intervention, and the A/C was kept within operational limits and VFR throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained positive and smooth A/C control with exceptional accuracy in all flight phases, handling the aileron, elevator and rudder trim with ease through the full airspeed range. Deviations were negligible, with altitude held within 40 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees. All A/C levers and switches were used without any difficulty, no procedure was skipped, and the required distance from clouds was maintained throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to pitch and bank inputs made without reference to the horizon and without trimming the A/C, did not maintain positive and smooth A/C control during the turns up to 60 degrees of bank. Altitude excursions reached 500 feet and the airspeed 35 knots above the briefed value, with the result that the IP took the controls to keep the A/C within operational limits. The basic control and trim sequence must be reflown before advancing.

SP, due to a false attitude perception that was not resolved against the instruments, did not compare the control and performance indications with the A/C positioning in space during the reversal. The A/C rolled 20 degrees past the briefed bank and lost 450 feet with the airspeed 30 knots high, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls and completed the recovery. Immediate transition to the instruments when the external attitude cue is doubtful is required.

SP, due to an incomplete trim sequence in which the rudder trim was not reset after the power changes, did not maintain positive and smooth A/C control and held constant control pressures in straight and level flight. The exit heading was 10 degrees off and the altitude 300 feet high, with the result that the parameters were regained only after the IP's verbal indications, with recognition and correction delayed. No IP control input was needed.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross check while attention remained outside the cockpit, did not locate the developing airspeed and altitude deviations in time. Airspeed decayed 20 knots below the briefed value and altitude reached 300 feet low in the turn, with the result that the corrections were applied late and only after the IP's verbal indications. Re-establishing a regular scan of the control and performance instruments is expected.

SP, due to trim applied only after the deviation had developed rather than during the airspeed change, did not maintain the smooth A/C control required in turns up to 60 degrees of bank. Altitude deviations of 200 feet and exit headings 8 degrees off the briefed value resulted, recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Trimming during, and not after, the airspeed change is expected.

SP, due to an aircraft state that had diverged from the SP's mental model without being reassessed, did not compare the instrument indications with the A/C positioning in space at the entry of the second turn. The airspeed was allowed to build 15 knots above the briefed value with the altitude 250 feet high, with the result of a deviation recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner, without IP's intervention. Reassessment of the A/C state at each maneuver entry is expected.

SP maintained basic A/C control within the desired standards, trimming the A/C and executing the corresponding corrections without IP's intervention. Altitude reached 140 feet off and airspeed 9 knots off on two occasions in turns up to 60 degrees of bank, at the edge of the desired standard, with exit headings within 5 degrees. Marginal performance for the Training Section - the deviations reduced in the later repetitions, and a faster cross check between the control and performance instruments is expected to improve the accuracy of the parameters.

SP maintained positive and smooth A/C control with exceptional accuracy in all flight phases, handling the aileron, elevator and rudder trim with ease and without any difficulty through the full airspeed range. Altitude was held within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees in straight and level flight and in turns up to 60 degrees of bank. The cross check was continuous, erroneous instrument readings were located in time and reported to the IP, and the A/C was kept well within operational limits and VFR throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.
